# timelib port: research, decision and status

Investigation behind `crates/twig-timelib`, the Rust port of timelib 2022.17 as PHP 8.5.13 uses it
(`PHPSRC/ext/date/lib`; PHP-side usage in `reference/php/stdlib.md` §13). `PHPSRC`/`TWIG` are defined in
`reference/target.md`.

**Decision: pure-Rust port, with both re2c scanners generated by re2c's Rust backend (re2rust 4.1) from timelib's own
`.re` files.** Binding the C library is not needed. Evidence in §3; status in §5 (everything PHP's `ext/date` needs
from timelib is ported, except the sunrise/sunset code, and verified against PHP and against the C library).

## 1. What PHP needs from timelib

### 1.1 Files (`PHPSRC/ext/date/lib`, `TIMELIB_ASCII_VERSION "2022.17"`)

| File | Lines | Bytes | Contents | Needed by |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `parse_date.re` | 2,791 | 79,303 | re2c source: `timelib_strtotime()` scanner (96 named sub-patterns, 50 active rules + 1 commented out), `timelib_parse_from_format[_with_map]()`, `timelib_parse_zone()`, `timelib_fill_holes()`, abbreviation search, relative-unit/month/day tables | `strtotime()`, `date_parse()`, `DateTime::__construct()`/`modify()`, `DateInterval::createFromDateString()`, `createFromFormat()`, `DateTimeZone::__construct()`, `timezone_name_from_abbr()`, `timezone_abbreviations_list()` |
| `parse_date.c` | 25,641 | 529,808 | committed re2c **1.0.3** output of the above (`-b`) | (generated) |
| `parse_iso_intervals.re` | 453 | 10,639 | re2c source of `timelib_strtointerval()` (ISO 8601 durations, combined form, start/end dates, `R<n>`) | `new DateInterval('P1D')`, `DatePeriod` ISO strings |
| `parse_iso_intervals.c` | 1,095 | 24,472 | committed re2c 1.0.3 output | (generated) |
| `parse_tz.c` | 973 | 26,845 | tzfile reader (`timelib_parse_tzfile()`), index search, `timelib_fetch_timezone_offset()`, `timelib_get_time_zone_info()`, offset info, `timelib_get_current_offset()`, `timelib_tzinfo_clone()` | every zone-aware operation, `DateTimeZone::getTransitions()`/`getLocation()`, `timezone_identifiers_list()` |
| `parse_posix.c` | 567 | 13,283 | POSIX TZ footer parser and yearly transitions | instants after a zone's last stored transition |
| `tm2unixtime.c` | 486 | 15,311 | `timelib_update_ts()`: normalisation, relative arithmetic (`+1 month` overflow, weekdays, "first/last day of"), local → UTC with the DST gap/overlap rules | every parse, `modify()`, `add()`/`sub()`, `setDate()`/`setTime()`/`setISODate()` |
| `unixtime2tm.c` | 247 | 6,829 | `timelib_unixtime2gmt()`/`unixtime2local()`, `update_from_sse()`, `set_timezone*()` | `new DateTime('@ts')`, `setTimezone()`, `setTimestamp()`, formatting |
| `interval.c` | 389 | 11,377 | `timelib_diff()`, `timelib_diff_days()`, `timelib_add()`/`sub()` (civil) and `add_wall()`/`sub_wall()` | `DateTime::diff()`, `add()`, `sub()` |
| `dow.c` | 216 | 6,307 | day of week/year, days in month, ISO week/date, validity checks | `format()` letters `D l N w z W o t`, parser checks |
| `timelib.c` | 391 | 10,682 | ctor/dtor/clone, `timelib_time_compare()`, `timelib_date_to_int()`, case-insensitive compare, decimal-hour helpers, error messages, debug dumps | everywhere |
| `timelib.h`, `timelib_private.h` | 1,104 + 188 | 38,622 + 4,930 | structs (`timelib_time`, `timelib_rel_time`, `timelib_tzinfo`, ...), constants, error codes | everywhere |
| `timezonemap.h`, `fallbackmap.h` | 1,127 + 42 | 65,377 + 1,973 | abbreviation tables: 1,127 name entries, 42 offset/DST fallback entries | zone abbreviations in parsed strings, `timezone_abbreviations_list()`, `timezone_name_from_abbr()` |
| `timezonedb.h` | 70,723 | 6,481,653 | embedded tz database `"2026.6"`, 598 entries, two variants: slim (`#ifdef TIMELIB_SUPPORT_SLIM_FILE`, 356,818 bytes of data) and fat | all zone data; `parse_tz.c` defines `TIMELIB_SUPPORT_SLIM_FILE` before including it, so PHP uses the slim variant |
| `astro.c`, `astro.h` | 313 + 74 | 11,716 + 4,144 | sunrise/sunset | only `date_sun_info()`, `date_sunrise()`, `date_sunset()`: **not needed by Twig, not ported** |

### 1.2 timelib entry points called by `PHPSRC/ext/date/php_date.c`

Counted with `grep -o 'timelib_[a-z0-9_]*(' php_date.c`, memory management left out: `timelib_update_ts` (19 call
sites), `timelib_time_clone` (13), `timelib_date_to_int` (13), `timelib_unixtime2local` (12), `timelib_strtotime` (9),
`timelib_rel_time_clone` (8), `timelib_day_of_week` (8), `timelib_get_time_zone_info` (6), `timelib_day_of_year` (6),
`timelib_unixtime2gmt` (5), `timelib_update_from_sse` (4), `timelib_timezone_id_is_valid` (3),
`timelib_isoweek_from_date` (3), `timelib_unixtime2date`, `timelib_strtointerval`, `timelib_set_timezone_from_offset`,
`timelib_parse_from_format`, `timelib_iso_day_of_week`, `timelib_is_leap`, `timelib_fill_holes`, `timelib_diff`,
`timelib_days_in_month` (2 each), `timelib_valid_date`, `timelib_timezone_identifiers_list`,
`timelib_timezone_id_from_abbr`, `timelib_timezone_abbreviations_list`, `timelib_time_compare`, `timelib_sub_wall`,
`timelib_sub`, `timelib_set_timezone_from_abbr`, `timelib_set_timezone`, `timelib_parse_zone`, `timelib_parse_tzfile`,
`timelib_get_transitions_for_year`, `timelib_get_current_offset` (sunrise/sunset only), `timelib_daynr_from_weeknr`,
`timelib_add_wall`, `timelib_add` (1 each), plus `timelib_astro_rise_set_altitude` (5, sun functions). Everything
else in timelib is internal to these.

### 1.3 Dependencies between the parts

```
parse_date.re ──► timelib.c (strcasecmp, ctor), dow.c (valid_date/time, daynr_from_weeknr, date_from_isodate),
      │           timezonemap.h + fallbackmap.h (abbr_search), tz_get_wrapper ──► parse_tz.c
      ▼
tm2unixtime.c ──► dow.c, unixtime2tm.c (date_from_epoch_days, set_timezone), parse_tz.c (offset info)
interval.c ─────► tm2unixtime.c (update_ts, do_rel_normalize, do_normalize), unixtime2tm.c, parse_tz.c
parse_tz.c ─────► parse_posix.c ──► unixtime2tm.c (unixtime2gmt), timezonedb.h (data)
parse_iso_intervals.re ──► parse_date.re's timelib_get_nr() (identical copy), timelib.c
```

The zone database, the calendar arithmetic and the interval code do not depend on the scanners, so they could be
ported and verified first (task step 2); the scanners sit on top.

### 1.4 Build configuration that matters

PHP compiles timelib with **`-fwrapv`** (`PHPSRC/ext/date/config0.m4`: `PHP_TIMELIB_CFLAGS="$PHP_TIMELIB_CFLAGS
-fwrapv"`), so signed overflow wraps instead of being undefined. The port uses wrapping arithmetic wherever input can
reach the edges, and `i32` wrapping where C computes in `int` (`z + dst * 3600`, `-z - dst * SECS_PER_HOUR`, ...).
Other configuration: `HAVE_STRTOLL` (same behaviour as `strtol` on LP64), `__builtin_saddll_overflow` available
(gcc ≥ 5: relative-unit overflow is reported as "Number out of range"), `MAX_ABBR_LEN` = `_POSIX_TZNAME_MAX` = 6
on glibc (every name in `timezonemap.h` has at most 4 bytes, so any value above 4 behaves the same), LP64 (64-bit
`timelib_long`), x86-64 double→integer conversion (`INT_MIN`/`INT64_MIN` for NaN and out-of-range values).

## 2. Licences

- timelib: MIT (`PHPSRC/ext/date/lib/LICENSE.rst`: Copyright (c) 2015-2021 Derick Rethans, Copyright (c)
  2017-2019,2021 MongoDB, Inc.; file headers extend the years to 2026). A port is a derivative work: the crate is
  licensed MIT (`crates/twig-timelib/Cargo.toml`) and carries timelib's notice in
  `crates/twig-timelib/LICENSE-timelib`. The workspace `NOTICE` must list it before publishing (roadmap "Workspace
  layout").
- Zone data: IANA tz database (public domain), packaged by timelib into `timezonedb.h`.
- re2c/re2rust: the generator is public domain; generated code carries no licence of its own. The generated
  `scanner.rs` files are derived from `parse_date.re`/`parse_iso_intervals.re` (MIT, as above).
- No PHP-licensed code is ported into the crate: `php_date.c` (PHP License 3.01) is only read to know how timelib is
  called. The test-only emulation of the PHP layer in `crates/twig-timelib/tests/common/mod.rs` and the C harness
  re-implement the few calling sequences needed for testing.

## 3. Experiment: can re2c's Rust backend generate the scanner?

### 3.1 Setup

- `docker/Dockerfile`: `debian:trixie-slim` + `apt install re2c gcc libc6-dev make` → **re2c 4.1** (Debian package
  `4.1-1`; `re2rust` is the same program's Rust mode), gcc 14.2.0. Image name `twig-timelib-tools`.
- Input: `PHPSRC/ext/date/lib/parse_date.re` in a copy whose C actions are translated to Rust:
  - the sub-pattern definitions block (`/*!re2c ... */` inside `scan()`, 96 named patterns) is copied **byte for
    byte** by `crates/twig-timelib/tools/gen_scanner_re.py`;
  - the rules block is `crates/twig-timelib/tools/scanner_rules.re.rs`: the 50 rule patterns are verbatim and in
    upstream order (checked mechanically: 50/50 identical; the commented-out `gnunocolontz` rule stays commented
    out), each C action translated line by line into Rust calling the ported helpers (`timelib_get_nr()` →
    `get_nr()`, `TIMELIB_HAVE_TIME()` → `have_time!`, ...);
  - re2c configuration for Rust: `re2c:api = custom`, `YYPEEK = s.str[cursor]`, `YYSKIP`, `YYBACKUP`/`YYRESTORE`
    on a `marker`, `YYLESSTHAN = s.lim - cursor < @@{len}`, `YYFILL = return EOI;` (timelib's
    `#define YYFILL(n) return EOI;`), `re2c:unsafe = 0` (bounds-checked indexing, no `unsafe`), and
    `/*!max:re2c*/` emitting `YYMAXFILL`. The input is padded with `YYMAXFILL` NUL bytes exactly like
    `timelib_strtotime()` pads it, so the fill/EOI behaviour near the end of the input is the C behaviour.
- Generation: `re2rust -b --no-generation-date -W -o scanner.rs scanner.re` (`-b` = bit vectors, as the committed C
  scanners were generated); script `crates/twig-timelib/tools/regen_scanner.sh <PHPSRC>/ext/date/lib`.
- The same procedure was then applied to `parse_iso_intervals.re` (`tools/gen_iso_scanner_re.py`,
  `tools/iso_scanner_rules.re.rs`).

### 3.2 Results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| re2rust accepts the verbatim definitions and rules | yes, for both files, no warnings with `-W` |
| `YYMAXFILL` | 36 (`parse_date`) and 20 (`parse_iso_intervals`), identical to the committed re2c 1.0.3 C scanners and to re2c 4.1's C output |
| Generated code | `src/parse_date/scanner.rs`: 53,694 lines, 1.93 MB; `src/parse_iso_intervals/scanner.rs`: 1,555 lines. One `loop`/`match` state machine each (Rust has no `goto`), safe Rust, only `panic!("internal lexer error")` in the unreachable default state |
| Reproducible | re-running `tools/regen_scanner.sh` reproduces both committed `scanner.re`/`scanner.rs` byte for byte |
| Compiles | yes, stable Rust 1.100, edition 2024, no `unsafe`, clippy clean (the generated functions carry `allow`s; `#[rustfmt::skip]` keeps them byte-identical to the generator output) |
| Build cost (this machine, crate only, clean) | debug 68 s, release 46 s, dominated by the one 53k-line function; dependants and incremental builds are unaffected |
| re2c version drift (C vs C) | re2c 4.1's C output of the unchanged `parse_date.re` and the committed re2c 1.0.3 `parse_date.c`, each linked into the C harness, give byte-identical dumps on 2,332,327 lines of the differential corpus (§4.2) |
| Rust scanner vs C timelib | byte-identical dumps on every differential input (§4.2) |

`reference/php/stdlib.md` §13.6 had rated a hand port of the parser "XL" and binding the C library "the pragmatic
route". With re2rust the scanners are generated from the unmodified upstream patterns, so the hand-written parser
code is limited to the ~875 lines of translated actions plus the helpers in `parse_date/mod.rs` and
`parse_iso_intervals/mod.rs` (themselves line-by-line ports), all checked against the C library.

### 3.3 Decision

**Pure-Rust port (preferred route) taken.** Reasons:

1. The generated scanners are exact by construction (same patterns, same rule order, same `YYMAXFILL`), and their
   actions are verified against the C original by differential testing on 2.3 million inputs with 98% line coverage
   of `parse_date.re` (the rest is unreachable, §4.3).
2. No C toolchain at build time (the PCRE2 crate already needs one; dates would have added a second C library and a
   Windows/MSVC build of re2c-generated C), no `unsafe` (workspace rule: only `twig-pcre` may use it).
3. `Send + Sync` zone data shared through `Arc`, no global C state (timelib's C API hands out heap structs the caller
   must free; PHP caches zones per request).
4. Upgrading: `.re` changes are picked up by regenerating; only changed actions need hand translation, and the
   harness shows any divergence.

Costs and risks: a 1.9 MB generated file (committed; building does not need re2c) with a noticeable compile time;
translation errors could hide in the few action lines no corpus reaches (all of them shown to be dead code, §4.3);
timelib upgrades need the regeneration step and a harness run.

Fallback (not needed): compile `PHPSRC/ext/date/lib/*.c` with `cc` and wrap `timelib_strtotime()` etc. in a safe
API; the C harness in `harness/` shows the build works (gcc 14, `-O2 -fwrapv`).

## 4. Verification

### 4.1 Oracle vectors (PHP 8.5.13 in Docker, committed, run by `cargo test -p twig-timelib`)

`crates/twig-timelib/tests/vectors/*.json`, generated by the `*.gen.php` scripts next to them
(`tests/vectors/regen.sh`, image `twig-oracle:3.31.1`); the PHP layer each vector passes through
(`php_date_initialize()`, `php_date_modify()`, `timezone_initialize()`, `date_interval_initialize()`, the setters,
the `format()` letters used) is emulated in `tests/common/mod.rs`. All 83,478 cases pass.

| File | Cases | What |
|---|---:|---|
| `parse.json` | 9,000 + 6,000 | `date_parse()` (all fields, warnings/errors with positions, zone, relative part) on php-src's `ext/date/tests` literals + random token strings; `date_parse_from_format()` |
| `strtotime.json` | 12,000 + 12,000 + 4,200 | `strtotime()` in 18 zones and 16 base times; `DateTime::modify()` incl. exception messages (`'2021-01-31 +1 month'` → `2021-03-03`); `new DateTime(wall clock, zone)` around DST transitions in 28 zones (local → UTC) |
| `interval.json` | 4,000 + 4,000 | `DateTime::diff()` (offset, abbreviation and id zones, microseconds); `add()`/`sub()` with wall (`new DateInterval`) and civil (`createFromDateString`) intervals |
| `zones.json` | 598 + 19,084 + 64 + 1,127 + 405 | identifier list and locations; local time (`Y n j G i s Z I T N z W o t L`) in every zone around transitions 1900-2100, far past/future and random 64-bit instants (UTC → local); `getTransitions()` samples; `timezone_abbreviations_list()`; `timezone_name_from_abbr()` |
| `iso_interval.json` | 5,000 | `new DateInterval($spec)`: durations, combined form, start/end dates, recurrences, broken strings, both exception messages |
| `setters.json` | 6,000 | `setDate()`, `setTime()`, `setISODate()`, `setTimestamp()` within hours of real transitions (DST gaps/overlaps) and with wide out-of-range field values |

### 4.2 Differential harness against the C library

`harness/harness.c` links PHP 8.5.13's own timelib sources (`PHPSRC/ext/date/lib/*.c`, built like PHP builds them:
`-O2 -fwrapv -DHAVE_STRTOLL`) and prints a canonical dump (every `timelib_time`/`timelib_rel_time`/`timelib_tzinfo`
field, every error/warning with code, position and character) per input line;
`crates/twig-timelib/examples/timelib_dump.rs` prints the same format from the port. `tools/gen_corpus.py` generates
the inputs, `run-differential.sh` runs everything (fixed seeds) and compares; the Rust side is built in release mode
**with overflow checks**, so an unintended arithmetic overflow would abort the run.

Result of `run-differential.sh` (this revision): **2,332,333 lines, 0 differences**, no overflow panic. Per harness
command (the `trans`, `extreme` and `special` generator modes emit commands of the other kinds):

| Command | What it exercises | Lines |
|---|---|---:|
| `parse` | `timelib_strtotime()` (php-src test literals, token sequences, random bytes, near-limit values) | 319,796 |
| `init` | `php_date_initialize()`: strtotime + `fill_holes` + `update_ts` + `update_from_sse` | 259,729 |
| `modify` | `php_date_modify()` | 249,671 |
| `format` | `timelib_parse_from_format()` | 200,032 |
| `local` | `timelib_unixtime2local()` in all 598 zones | 299,626 |
| `fmtinit` | `createFromFormat()`: parse_from_format + `fill_holes(OVERRIDE_TIME)` + update | 100,000 |
| `zone` | `timezone_initialize()`: `timelib_parse_zone()` on ids, abbreviations, offsets, junk | 20,000 |
| `diff` | `timelib_diff()`, `timelib_diff_days()` | 150,031 |
| `add` | `timelib_add()`/`sub()`/`add_wall()`/`sub_wall()` with parsed and field intervals | 140,071 |
| `mk` | setDate/setTime/setISODate/setTimestamp paths, `timelib_get_current_offset()` | 140,334 |
| `info` | `timelib_get_time_zone_info()`, offset info, `timestamp_is_in_dst()`, POSIX transitions | 59,800 |
| `tzfile` | `timelib_parse_tzfile()` field by field for every zone + case variants, `timezone_id_is_valid()` | 3,000 |
| `dow` | all of `dow.c`, epoch-day conversions (including 64-bit extremes) | 100,220 |
| `abbr` | `timelib_timezone_id_from_abbr()` | 20,000 |
| `ival` | `timelib_strtointerval()` | 50,002 |
| `raw` | `update_ts`/`update_from_sse`/`unixtime2local` on unfilled parse results (zone type none, UNSET fields) | 60,000 |
| `posix` | `timelib_parse_posix_str()` on valid and broken strings, transitions incl. Julian forms | 30,021 |
| `hms` | decimal-hour helpers (incl. NaN/∞/huge), `hms_to_seconds()`, error messages | 30,000 |
| `formatx` | `timelib_parse_from_format_with_map()` with prefix `%` and the ISO-week/year/minutes specifiers | 100,000 |

Generator modes (`tools/gen_corpus.py`, counts and seeds in `run-differential.sh`): one per command above, plus
`trans` (200,000 diff/add/mk/init/modify lines within hours of real transitions of 16 zones, taken from
`zones.json`), `extreme` (60,000 lines with amounts, dates and base times near the 64-bit limits) and `special`
(533 fixed cases: more than 1000 errors, overflowing relative amounts, an expanded year equal to `TIMELIB_UNSET`,
embedded NUL bytes in formats, NNBSP in log dates, ISO weeks past the end of the year, broken POSIX strings).

The corpus (in its 2,332,327-line state, before the last six `special` format cases were added) run through a C
harness whose `parse_date.c` was regenerated by re2c 4.1 instead of the committed re2c 1.0.3 file gives output
byte-identical to the committed scanner's.

### 4.3 Coverage of the C code by the corpora

`harness/coverage.sh` rebuilds the harness with `--coverage` and runs the same corpus (`run-differential.sh
... --coverage`, summary by `tools/gcov_summary.py`):

| Upstream file | Lines executed | Not executed |
|---|---:|---|
| `parse_date.re` (actions + helpers) | 1,292 / 1,314 (98.3%) | dead code only: zone parsing inside `timelong24`/`iso8601nocolon` (their patterns contain no zone), zone-not-found branches after `tzcorrection`-only patterns (always found), fraction branches after patterns without fractions, `timelib_get_frac_nr()`/`timelib_get_relative_text()` skip loops (callers always start at a digit/letter), `timelib_set_relative()` unknown-unit return (patterns only admit known units), the 1000-warnings cap (at most 3 warnings exist), `errors == NULL` branches (PHP always passes a container), `timelib_timezone_abbreviations_list()` (compared to PHP's list by the oracle instead) |
| `parse_iso_intervals.re` | 187 / 194 (96.4%) | sign handling and "no number" returns in `timelib_get_unsigned_nr()` (patterns contain no signs and always digits), `errors == NULL` |
| `tm2unixtime.c`, `interval.c`, `dow.c` | 100% | |
| `unixtime2tm.c` | 116 / 124 (93.5%) | `timelib_apply_localtime()` (unused by PHP), a `free()` |
| `parse_posix.c` | 247 / 250 (98.8%) | a failure exit that a preceding check makes impossible, the default case of `calc_transition()`, one malformed-week exit |
| `parse_tz.c` | 292 / 511 (57.1%) | code the embedded database cannot reach: plain `TZif` files, version 4, leap seconds, corrupt-file errors, zones without a POSIX string, `timelib_dump_tzinfo()`, `timelib_tzinfo_clone()` (PHP always passes `TIMELIB_NO_CLONE`), `timelib_timezone_identifiers_list()` |
| `timelib.c` | 106 / 179 (59.2%) | debug dumps (`timelib_dump_date()`, `timelib_dump_rel_time()`), ctor/dtor helpers, `timelib_get_tz_abbr_ptr()` (not called by PHP) |
| `parse_date.c` (generated DFA, re2c 1.0.3) | 11,046 / 16,288 (67.8%) | DFA transitions; the Rust DFA is generated by re2c 4.1 from the same patterns, and re2c 1.0.3 vs 4.1 equivalence was checked on the differential corpus (§3.2) |

## 5. Status

### 5.1 Ported and verified (crate `twig-timelib`)

| Module | timelib source | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| `types` | `timelib.h` structs, constants, error codes, `timelib_time_compare()`, `timelib_date_to_int()`, `timelib_time_tz_abbr_update()` | harness (all commands dump the structs) |
| `dow` | `dow.c` (all functions) | harness `dow`/`mk`, oracle `zones` (N z W o t L) |
| `unixtime2tm` | `unixtime2tm.c` (all; `timelib_apply_localtime()` is ported but never exercised, PHP does not call it) | harness `local`/`raw`/`mk`, oracle `zones` |
| `tm2unixtime` | `tm2unixtime.c` (all) | harness, oracle `strtotime`/`setters` |
| `interval` | `interval.c` (all), `timelib_same_timezone()` | harness `diff`/`add`/`trans`, oracle `interval` |
| `tz` | `parse_tz.c` (reader, lookups, offsets, `timelib_get_current_offset()`, clone, error messages); embedded slim `timezonedb.h` 2026.6 verbatim (`tzdb/timezonedb.bin`, 356,818 bytes, + `tzdb/index.rs`) | harness `tzfile`/`info`/`local`, oracle `zones` (locations, transitions, local times in all 598 zones) |
| `posix` | `parse_posix.c` (all) | harness `posix`/`info`, oracle `zones` |
| `abbr` | `timezonemap.h`, `fallbackmap.h` (generated `abbr_data.rs`), `abbr_search()`, `timelib_timezone_id_from_abbr()`, `timelib_timezone_abbreviations_list()` | harness `abbr`/`zone`, oracle `zones` |
| `parse_date` | `parse_date.re`: scanner (generated), all actions and helpers, `timelib_strtotime()`, `timelib_parse_zone()`, `timelib_parse_from_format[_with_map]()`, `timelib_fill_holes()` | harness, oracle `parse`/`strtotime` |
| `parse_iso_intervals` | `parse_iso_intervals.re`: scanner (generated), actions, `timelib_strtointerval()` | harness `ival`, oracle `iso_interval` |
| `timelib` | `timelib.c` helpers (`strcasecmp`, `strncasecmp`, decimal hours, `hms_to_seconds`) | harness `hms` |

### 5.2 Not ported (with reasons)

- `astro.c` (`timelib_astro_rise_set_altitude()`): only `date_sun_info()`/`date_sunrise()`/`date_sunset()` use it;
  Twig cannot reach them.
- Debug output (`timelib_dump_date()`, `timelib_dump_rel_time()`, `timelib_dump_tzinfo()`) and
  `timelib_get_tz_abbr_ptr()`: not called by PHP.
- Memory management (`*_ctor`/`*_dtor`, `timelib_strdup`, ...): replaced by Rust ownership (`Clone`, `Arc<TzInfo>`).
- Reading zone files from disk / system tzdata: PHP 8.5.13's official image uses the embedded database only.

### 5.3 Deviations

None observable through PHP. Port-level differences, all documented in the code: zone data is shared through
`Arc` and `TIMELIB_NO_CLONE` is implied (without it `timelib_tzinfo_clone()` is used, as in C); a zone-id time
without zone data is treated as "no zone" where C would dereference `NULL`; table lookups clamp month indexes that
C would read out of bounds (unreachable from PHP); `parse_iso_intervals.re`'s `add_error()` leaves the C error code
uninitialised, the port stores 0 (PHP only looks at the error count).

### 5.4 Not part of this crate (later stages)

The PHP layer in `php_date.c` (PHP License) is ported elsewhere: `DateTime::format()` letters
(`reference/php/stdlib.md` §13.3), `DateInterval::format()` (§13.4), property tables/`var_dump` (§13.5), the
`DateTime`/`DateTimeZone`/`DateInterval` objects with their exception and warning texts, `getTransitions()` (note
its `size_t` year loop), `getLocation()`, `php_date_initialize()`/`php_date_modify()` (case-insensitive `"now"`
shortcut, `@ts` resets the zone to UTC). `crates/twig-timelib/tests/common/mod.rs` shows the calling sequences
those wrappers must use.

## 6. Files and how to re-run

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `docker/Dockerfile` | tool image `twig-timelib-tools`: re2c 4.1 (re2rust) + gcc 14 |
| `run-differential.sh` | `run-differential.sh <php-src> <workdir> [--coverage]`: corpora, C harness, Rust dump, comparison |
| `harness/harness.c`, `harness/run.sh` | C side of the differential test (links PHP's timelib, `-O2 -fwrapv`) |
| `harness/coverage.sh` | gcov build and run of the C side |
| `tools/gen_corpus.py` | corpus generator (22 modes, fixed seeds) |
| `tools/compare_outputs.py`, `tools/gcov_summary.py` | comparison and coverage summaries |
| `crates/twig-timelib/tools/regen_scanner.sh` | regenerates both scanners (`gen_scanner_re.py` + `scanner_rules.re.rs`, `gen_iso_scanner_re.py` + `iso_scanner_rules.re.rs`) |
| `crates/twig-timelib/tools/gen_tzdb.py`, `gen_abbr.py` | zone database and abbreviation table conversion |
| `crates/twig-timelib/tests/vectors/regen.sh` | regenerates the oracle vectors (`*.gen.php`) |
| `crates/twig-timelib/examples/timelib_dump.rs` | Rust side of the differential test |
